subThemes.name: Grid hardware and automation
subThemes.description: Equipment that moves, protects and automates electricity networks, such as transformers, switchgear and control systems.

subThemes.name: Energy efficiency and demand
subThemes.description: Products and software that cut energy use in buildings and industry, or shift demand in response to grid signals.

subThemes.name: Storage and flexibility
subThemes.description: Batteries, inverters and balancing services that let grids absorb variable renewable supply.

kpis.name: Grid and automation revenue share
kpis.definition: Share of the latest annual revenue earned from electrical grid equipment, grid automation and related services.

rubric.level0: No disclosed grid or automation revenue.
rubric.level1: Grid products are mentioned but under 10 percent of revenue.
rubric.level2: Grid products are 10 to 25 percent of revenue.
rubric.level3: Grid products are 25 to 50 percent of revenue, with a segment figure.
rubric.level4: Grid products are over 50 percent of revenue, with a segment figure.
rubric.unknownRule: Answer unknown when the filing gives no revenue split that identifies grid products.

extraction.target: Revenue from grid equipment, grid automation and related services divided by total revenue for the latest fiscal year, from the segment or product revenue note.

kpis.name: R&D intensity
kpis.definition: Research and development expense divided by revenue, as a proxy for investment in new energy technology.

kpis.name: Storage and flexibility commitment
kpis.definition: How strongly the company commits capital and products to batteries, inverters or grid balancing, beyond statements of intent.

rubric.level0: No storage or flexibility activity is described.
rubric.level1: Storage is named as an opportunity with no commitment.
rubric.level2: A pilot or small product line exists without capital figures.
rubric.level3: A commercial product or project is described with some figures.
rubric.level4: Storage is a core business with capital committed and revenue figures.
rubric.unknownRule: Answer unknown when the text gives too little to separate intent from commitment.

kpis.name: Efficiency product exposure
kpis.definition: Extent to which core products reduce customer energy use, such as drives, controls and building automation.

rubric.level0: No product linked to energy savings.
rubric.level1: Energy savings are a minor marketing point.
rubric.level2: Some products have stated energy savings.
rubric.level3: Most products are sold on measured energy savings.
rubric.level4: The company is defined by efficiency products with measured savings.
rubric.unknownRule: Answer unknown when product descriptions do not mention energy use at all.

kpis.name: Scale by market capitalisation
kpis.definition: Market capitalisation in US dollars, to favour companies large enough to deliver at grid scale.

rationale: Grid equipment is the core of smart energy, so it carries the largest weight and is the gate. Efficiency and storage are scored on rubrics. Two quant KPIs add scale and investment.
